Based on the retrieved healthcare Q&A matches, it appears that there is evidence suggesting that ultrasound-scored synovitis in patients with rheumatoid arthritis does not significantly depend on the pharmacokinetics of subcutaneous anti-TNF (anti-tumor necrosis factor) agents. 

Several studies have investigated this topic, and the findings indicate that s.c. anti-TNF pharmacokinetics do not influence US (ultrasound)-scored synovitis in RA patients. For instance, one study found no significant difference in ultrasound-scored synovitis between patients who received placebo or a specific anti-TNF medication with good pharmacokinetics.

Another study suggested that the effectiveness of s.c. anti-TNF agents may not be influenced by their pharmacokinetics, as indicated by an improved US score among patients on these medications compared to those receiving placebo.

However, it is essential to note that individual responses to treatment can vary greatly, and more research is needed to fully understand the relationship between anti-TNF pharmacokinetics and ultrasound-scored synovitis in RA patients.
